TripleLift (3lift) is a programmatic SSP, not a chumbox. Knock-on: incentives.js uses vendors("native_ads")>0 as proof of ad slots.
tracker.native_ads.fix: Match by loader path: cdn.taboola.com/libtrc/unip/ and amplify.outbrain.com are advertiser pixels (→ advertising buy-side); /libtrc/<publisher>/loader.js and widgets.outbrain.com are publisher widgets (native_ads). Move triplelift/3lift, sharethrough, nativo to advertising.
tracker.native_ads.meaning: A chumbox of paid "recommended" links is on this page.

tracker.popup_capture.cause: Three of three right (Wunderkind on AP, OptinMonster on Salon and Cato); the vendors' product is the pop-up, so presence is proof of the service even before a pop-up shows.
tracker.popup_capture.fix: None. Pair with dark.interrupting_overlay when both fire so the chip reads "Pop-up (OptinMonster)".
tracker.popup_capture.meaning: Pop-ups here are a hosted service built to capture your email.

tracker.push_notifications.cause: Three of three are the OneSignal SDK on news sites, near-universal; SDK presence is not a prompt. surveillance.notification_preprompt is the real check.
tracker.push_notifications.fix: Severity 0, no chip; mention the vendor inside notification_preprompt when that fires.
tracker.push_notifications.meaning: The site can prompt you for browser notifications.

tracker.session_replay.cause: Three of three right (Crazy Egg, FullStory, Microsoft Clarity on a donation form). All listed vendors record sessions; the "some vendors also capture typing" hedge is accurate.
tracker.session_replay.fix: None. Raise prominence when a payment or password field is on the page (Clarity on MSF donate).
tracker.session_replay.meaning: Your mouse, scrolling and possibly typing are recorded for replay.

tracker.social_pixel.cause: Three of three right (Facebook pixel on AP and Vox, LinkedIn+Bing+Facebook on Canva). bat.bing.com is Microsoft Advertising, not social; label nit only.
tracker.social_pixel.fix: Rename the category "Ad-platform pixels"; name the platform in the why ("Meta learns you read this").
tracker.social_pixel.meaning: Meta/LinkedIn/Microsoft learn you visited, tied to your account.

tracker.third_party_volume.cause: Two of three right (NRA 28, ZDNet 53). Fires at ≥12 with a fixed why "Dozens of companies learned you're here": false at 12–23 (NPR 21). thirdParty counts fonts, CDNs, payment processors and CMPs, and evidence shows the first eight in load order (cookielaw.org, stripe.com, typekit.net), which undercuts the claim.
tracker.third_party_volume.fix: Subtract an infrastructure allowlist (fonts.gstatic, typekit, cloudfront, akamai, fastly, jsdelivr, cdnjs, stripe, paypal, cookielaw, onetrust, recaptcha, youtube-nocookie); why states the number ("31 other companies were contacted"); evidence lists categorised trackers first; severity 1 at ≥20, 2 at ≥40.
tracker.third_party_volume.meaning: N other companies received a request, with your IP, when this page loaded.

dark.preselection.cause: No checkout or sign-up form in the corpus. Direct observation (a checked box with a marketing label). Risk in code: PRECHECK_WORDS /cover|express|priority|updates/ match "discover", a pre-selected "Express" shipping radio, and radio groups must have a default.
dark.preselection.fix: Use \b boundaries; ignore radio inputs unless the label names a paid add-on. Show on first firing.
dark.preselection.meaning: A box was ticked for you before you chose.

dark.disguised_ads.cause: Never fired; the measurement (font <10px or contrast <3 on a "Sponsored" label) is direct. Depends on SHORT leaf elements ≤28 chars matching sponsoredLabels exactly.
dark.disguised_ads.fix: Show on first firing; quote the measured size/contrast in evidence.
dark.disguised_ads.meaning: The "Sponsored" label is too small or faint to notice.

dark.content_gate.cause: Never fired although Vox's membership wall was on a corpus page (caught as an overlay instead): gate selectors need paywall/regwall/piano class names and the blur check needs an <article> ancestor.
dark.content_gate.fix: Add [class*="wall" i],[class*="gate" i] with gateWords, and let the blur check run under main. Show on first firing with the blurred element quoted.
dark.content_gate.meaning: Part of the text is hidden behind a sign-up or subscription wall.

surveillance.notification_preprompt.cause: Never fired; the check (fixed/sticky element with "allow notifications" wording and an allow/enable word) is direct.
surveillance.notification_preprompt.fix: Show on first firing. Add the push vendor name from tracker.push_notifications when present.
surveillance.notification_preprompt.meaning: The site asks for notification permission before the browser does.

urgency.live_countdown.cause: Never fired despite Shein/Temu/Groupon in the corpus. checkTimers holds element references for 2.2 s; frameworks re-render timer nodes each tick so document.contains(f.el) fails; split-digit timers are found only under class names containing "countdown"/"timer".
urgency.live_countdown.fix: Re-run findTimerElements after observeMs and match by text/ancestor path, not identity; widen the split-digit selector to [class*="count" i],[class*="time" i],[aria-label*="count" i]. A ticking timer is a fact (show it), fakeness is the reset check.
urgency.live_countdown.meaning: A countdown is ticking on this page.

urgency.fake_countdown_reset.cause: Needs a second visit, so single-visit recordings cannot fire it. The strongest proof in the product: stored remaining time vs observed.
urgency.fake_countdown_reset.fix: Show on first firing. Store per path and per timer text so two timers on one page are not confused.
urgency.fake_countdown_reset.meaning: This deadline restarted on reload: it is manufactured.

dark.exit_intent_popup.cause: Offline replay has no mouse, so never fired. Behavioural proof (overlay within 1.5 s of mouseleave at the top edge). describeTrigger calls any overlay more than 800 ms after a click "timed", so a slow click-opened dialog could be misattributed.
dark.exit_intent_popup.fix: Raise the click window to 2 s and ignore overlays opened while focus is inside a button/link. Show on first firing.
dark.exit_intent_popup.meaning: A pop-up fired as you moved to leave.

dark.nagging.cause: Needs three separate overlays in one session; never reached. Count is direct.
dark.nagging.fix: Show on first firing; quote the three overlay texts.
dark.nagging.meaning: Three or more pop-ups interrupted this page.

attention.infinite_scroll.cause: Replay does not scroll. Measured page growth near the bottom is direct, but the code still emits (confidence 0.5) when a "load more" button exists, which is not infinite scroll.
attention.infinite_scroll.fix: Do not emit when loadMore is true. Show on first firing.
attention.infinite_scroll.meaning: The page keeps loading more as you scroll; no end.

attention.title_bait.cause: Never fired. Observed title change while hidden is direct, but /new|message|alert/ matches a headline swap ("New York…") on a news site.
attention.title_bait.fix: Require \(\d+\), an emoji, or come back|miss|don't; ignore changes that coincide with a URL change.
attention.title_bait.meaning: The tab title changes while you are away to pull you back.

charts.inverted_axis.cause: No inline SVG chart with ≥3 numeric labels in the corpus. Direct measurement when the y-axis grouping is right.
charts.inverted_axis.fix: Show on first firing with the top/bottom tick values quoted (already in explain).
charts.inverted_axis.meaning: Up means less on this chart.

charts.truncated_bar_axis.cause: Never fired. hasBars counts any ≥3 rects taller than 4 px (gridlines, backgrounds, legend swatches), so a zoomed line chart can be called a bar chart at severity 3.
charts.truncated_bar_axis.fix: Require bar rects to share a baseline y and have similar widths before calling it a bar chart.
charts.truncated_bar_axis.meaning: Bars start above zero, exaggerating differences.

charts.zoomed_line_axis.cause: Never fired; a zoomed line axis is a legitimate choice as often as a trick.
charts.zoomed_line_axis.meaning: The y-axis starts high, so small moves look large.

charts.unlabeled_log_scale.cause: Never fired. The first clause of `geometric` is a tautology (x - x < 1e-9); only the ratio test does the work, which is fine.
charts.unlabeled_log_scale.fix: Delete the dead clause; show on first firing.
charts.unlabeled_log_scale.meaning: Tick values multiply but nothing says "log scale".

charts.irregular_axis.cause: Never fired; direct measurement of value/pixel ratios across ticks.
charts.irregular_axis.fix: Show on first firing with the tick list quoted.
charts.irregular_axis.meaning: Equal gaps on the axis hold unequal values.

charts.dual_axis.cause: Never fired; two vertical tick groups far apart is a reasonable proxy.
charts.dual_axis.meaning: Two y-axes let any two lines appear to track.

charts.short_window.cause: Never fired; a ≤3-year x-axis is an opinion about scope, not a measured distortion.
charts.short_window.meaning: The chart covers three years or fewer.

charts.few_points.cause: Never fired; ≤4 x positions is not manipulation.

charts.pie.cause: Never fired; a pie chart is a chart type, not a technique. Severity 1 is an opinion.
charts.pie.meaning: A pie chart; check the slices sum to 100%.

charts.flat_aspect.cause: Never fired; aspect ratio >4.5 is common for sparklines and timelines.

charts.tall_aspect.cause: Never fired; an opinion about proportions.

charts.no_axis_titles.cause: Never fired; many honest charts carry units in the caption rather than the SVG.
charts.no_axis_titles.meaning: No units or axis titles inside the chart.

charts.no_source.cause: Never fired; it would fire on every chart whose source line is outside the three ancestors searched.
charts.no_source.fix: Severity 0 note; search the enclosing figure/article caption too.
charts.no_source.meaning: No data source cited near the chart.

charts.svg_chart_ok.cause: A non-finding ("passed basic checks") that would take a chip slot.
charts.svg_chart_ok.fix: Keep only as meta/asset for AI; no chip.
charts.svg_chart_ok.meaning: An SVG chart passed the axis checks.

tracker.social_proof_widget.cause: Never fired. Vendor presence is strong proof that activity toasts are generated, but trackers.json lists review platforms (yotpo, judge.me, stamped, loox, okendo) and Elfsight (generic widgets) under this severity-3 category; a Judge.me review widget is not "someone in Ohio just bought".
tracker.social_proof_widget.fix: Move review platforms to a reviews_widget note (severity 0) and Elfsight out; keep fomo/provesrc/useproof/nudgify/trustpulse/wisernotify and peers. Show on first firing.
tracker.social_proof_widget.meaning: The "someone just bought" toasts come from a vendor that makes them.

tracker.urgency_widget.cause: Never fired. Only deadlinefunnel/countdownhero/timify/hurrify/evergreencountdown/sentry-countdown sell evergreen timers; thrivecart/clickfunnels/kartra/samcart/leadpages/unbounce/instapage are funnel and landing-page builders whose presence proves nothing about a timer.
tracker.urgency_widget.fix: Split: timer vendors keep severity 3; funnel builders become a severity-0 "funnel builder" note. Show timer vendors on first firing.
tracker.urgency_widget.meaning: The countdown here is a vendor product that restarts per visitor.

tracker.bnpl.cause: Never fired in the pack; Klarna/Afterpay are on most shops, so when it fires it will be ordinary at severity 2.
tracker.bnpl.fix: Demote to severity 0; mention inside incentives.purchase_path as "pay-later offered".
tracker.bnpl.meaning: Instalment payments are offered on this page.

source.advocacy_no_funding_disclosure.cause: Never fired: transparency.js returns before this check when !isArticle, so organisation home pages, where it matters, never reach it; corpus think tanks are in the dataset anyway. Name-word heuristic plus an absence, not a proof.
source.advocacy_no_funding_disclosure.fix: Move the check above the isArticle return; require the name words in og:site_name or <title>, not the hostname alone.
source.advocacy_no_funding_disclosure.meaning: Presents as an institute or campaign; no funding link on the page.
